From faa72102b178c7ae6c6afea23879e7c84fc59b4e Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jason Gunthorpe <jgg@nvidia.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 11:02:50 -0400
Subject: [PATCH] RDMA/ionic: Fix kernel stack leak in ionic_create_cq()

struct ionic_cq_resp resp {
    __u32 cqid[2];         // offset 0 - PARTIALLY SET (see below)
    __u8  udma_mask;       // offset 8 - SET (resp.udma_mask = vcq->udma_mask)
    __u8  rsvd[7];         // offset 9 - NEVER SET <- LEAK
};

rsvd[7]: 7 bytes of stack memory leaked unconditionally.

cqid[2]: The loop at line 1256 iterates over udma_idx but skips indices
where !(vcq->udma_mask & BIT(udma_idx)). The array has 2 entries but
udma_count could be 1, meaning cqid[1] might never be written via
ionic_create_cq_common(). If udma_mask only has bit 0 set, cqid[1] (4
bytes) is also leaked. So potentially 11 bytes leaked.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: e8521822c733 ("RDMA/ionic: Register device ops for control path")
Signed-off-by: Jason Gunthorpe <jgg@nvidia.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/4-v1-83e918d69e73+a9-rdma_udata_rc_jgg@nvidia.com
Acked-by: Abhijit Gangurde <abhijit.gangurde@amd.com>
Signed-off-by: Leon Romanovsky <leon@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/infiniband/hw/ionic/ionic_controlpath.c b/drivers/infiniband/hw/ionic/ionic_controlpath.c
index 5b3f40bd98d8..4842931f5316 100644
--- a/drivers/infiniband/hw/ionic/ionic_controlpath.c
+++ b/drivers/infiniband/hw/ionic/ionic_controlpath.c
@@ -1218,7 +1218,7 @@ int ionic_create_cq(struct ib_cq *ibcq, const struct ib_cq_init_attr *attr,
 		rdma_udata_to_drv_context(udata, struct ionic_ctx, ibctx);
 	struct ionic_vcq *vcq = to_ionic_vcq(ibcq);
 	struct ionic_tbl_buf buf = {};
-	struct ionic_cq_resp resp;
+	struct ionic_cq_resp resp = {};
 	struct ionic_cq_req req;
 	int udma_idx = 0, rc;
 
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

### File: `drivers/infiniband/hw/ionic/ionic_controlpath.c`

- **Change**: In function `ionic_create_cq()`, the declaration of `struct ionic_cq_resp resp;` was modified to `struct ionic_cq_resp resp = {};`
  
  This zero-initializes the entire `resp` structure, ensuring all fields (including `rsvd[7]` and potentially unset entries in `cqid[2]`) are cleared before being copied to user space.

### Relationship Between Modifications

The single change directly addresses the kernel stack leak vulnerability. Previously, the `resp` structure was left uninitialized, which could cause up to 11 bytes of stack memory (7 bytes from `rsvd[7]` and 4 bytes from a possibly unset `cqid[1]`) to be exposed to user space via the RDMA control path. By zero-initializing `resp`, all unused or partially written fields are explicitly set to zero, eliminating the information leak. No other state or logic changes are needed.

Root cause:
The `ionic_cq_resp` structure in `ionic_create_cq()` is not fully initialized before being copied to user space. The `rsvd[7]` field is never set, and the `cqid[2]` array may have uninitialized entries if `udma_count` is less than 2 or if some indices are skipped based on `udma_mask`. This results in leaking up to 11 bytes of kernel stack memory to user space.

Code statements information:
The code statements that lead to the bug are:
struct ionic_cq_resp resp;
Reason: The `resp` structure is declared without initialization, so the `rsvd[7]` field is never set, and if the loop does not fill all `cqid[2]` entries (e.g., when `udma_mask` skips indices or `udma_count` is 1), uninitialized kernel stack bytes are leaked to userspace via `ib_copy_to_udata`.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
struct ionic_cq_resp resp = {};
Reason: Zero-initializing the entire structure ensures that all fields, including `rsvd` and any unwritten `cqid` entries, are set to zero, preventing the leak of uninitialized kernel stack memory.
